prompt: Three screens repeat read order, pack items and estimate delivery. What most directly simplifies their callers?

options.explanation: Shared lifetime does not remove the repeated sequence. It can add unwanted shared state.

options.text: A Facade exposing one preview_delivery operation.
options.explanation: The Facade coordinates the sequence behind one clear entry point. Its collaborators can still be injected and tested.

options.text: A Factory that only creates the reader.
options.explanation: That centralizes one creation decision but leaves all callers coordinating the repeated process.
The example is a read-only preview. Extra commits neither simplify the interface nor make the process atomic.

prompt: Three selected orders invoke Approve through one $batch. One order fails. What establishes whether the other two roll back together?

options.explanation: One batch can contain several independent changesets. The envelope alone does not prove atomic grouping.

options.text: The shared changeset, requested with #CHANGE_SET and verified in metadata, payload and a failure test.
options.explanation: InvocationGrouping configures the supporting UI. You must verify the actual common changeset and all-or-nothing persistence.

options.text: Adding COMMIT WORK in each action handler.
options.explanation: RAP owns commit. A provider-side COMMIT violates the transaction model instead of grouping requests.

options.text: Assuming #ISOLATED means no batching at all.
options.explanation: Isolated changesets may still travel together in a batch request.

prompt: A legacy BAPI always executes COMMIT WORK internally. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Moving it into save_modified makes the COMMIT legal.
options.explanation: A saver is still RAP provider code. Changing the save option does not transfer commit ownership to the BAPI.

options.text: Review or replace the API; neither BRFplus nor bgRFC automatically removes its transaction restrictions.
options.explanation: BRFplus is a rules engine; ordinary bgRFC units forbid COMMIT. A supported bgPF uncontrolled operation is a separate option for logic needing its own commit. It still needs explicit completion, retry and partial-failure handling outside the original RAP transaction.

options.text: Calling it through BRFplus guarantees one atomic LUW.
options.explanation: A rules engine is not a transaction isolation mechanism.

options.text: Any separate RFC can be rolled back by the original RAP transaction.
options.explanation: A separately committed remote operation cannot be undone by local rollback.
